content.text: The text combines excerpts from several works. In *Harry West*, Harry aids Joe Flint’s starving family, confronts Major Phillips, enters Wake & Wade’s Boston store, visits Julia Bryant in Rockville, and later is falsely accused of theft before his father, Franklin West, recognizes him in court. Harry ultimately becomes wealthy and marries Julia. A separate dance manual explains the Boston, its foot positions, partner formations, turns, and related dances. Other excerpts include advertisements and plays, an Irish article on goose-raising, and Robert Ingersoll’s speeches attacking religious dogma while praising science, liberty, education, humane government, labor, honest money, and intellectual freedom. He honors figures including Christ, Paine, Jefferson, Franklin, Humboldt, and Lincoln, and argues that morality should rest on reason, justice, compassion, and making others happy.
